frontmatter_description: Determine whether information should stay private or may be disclosed based on the disclosure boundary.
title: Privacy, Secrets, and Boundaries
use_when: Use when the task is to decide what information may be shared and what should remain private.
Use when the main variable is the disclosure boundary itself: secret, private fact, confidential detail, or off-limits topic.
Use when the question is about whether telling someone is allowed, appropriate, or too revealing.
do_not_use_when: Do not use when the main issue is repairing harm after the information was already revealed; use relationship repair instead.
Do not use when the main issue is self-presentation, image management, or choosing how to present oneself; use impression management instead.
Do not use when the main issue is role, status, identity group, or hierarchy rather than disclosure.
decision_variable: whether the information is within the disclosure boundary
trigger_checklist: Is the content a secret, private fact, or confidential detail?
Is the question asking whether it should be told, withheld, or kept within a defined audience?
Has the scene defined a boundary such as personal, family, professional, or relational confidentiality?
Is the key judgment about disclosure permission rather than apology, persuasion, or role?
workflow: Identify the item of information that might be shared.
Ask who is entitled to know it under the scene's boundary.
Check whether the information is private by default, explicitly shared, or already public.
If disclosure would cross the boundary, keep it private; if it is within the allowed circle, it may be shared.

special_case.title: Already Shared Means Exit to Repair
special_case.rule: If the information has already been revealed, this unit no longer applies; switch to repair, apology, or relationship recovery.

worked_example.scene: A friend accidentally tells another person a private diagnosis that was meant to stay secret.
worked_example.question: Should this unit decide what to do next?
worked_example.answer_logic: No. The boundary has already been crossed, so the active question is repair after disclosure, not whether the information may be shared.

boundary_exit_rule: Exit if the question is about how to apologize, explain, or restore trust after disclosure.
Exit if the question is about how to present oneself or control impressions rather than protect information.
Exit if the issue is role-based access, group identity, or power hierarchy rather than privacy.
Exit if the scene is mainly about lying, persuasion, or indirect meaning rather than confidentiality.

references.route_signal: Use this micro unit when the central diagnostic question is whether information crosses a privacy boundary.
hard_boundary: Does not handle repair after a boundary has already been crossed.
Does not decide how to apologize, explain, or reconcile after disclosure.
Does not judge overall self-image or audience impression.
shortcut_to_avoid: Do not treat every secret as a lie; a kept secret can be truthful withholding.
Do not jump to repair just because the disclosure feels awkward; first ask whether the boundary was actually crossed.
common_failure_modes: Confusing privacy with group membership or status.
Using apology logic when the only question is whether to disclose.

minimal_pair.case: A person refuses to repeat a friend's private medical issue to a coworker.
minimal_pair.why_it_matches: The answer depends on whether the medical detail is inside the disclosure boundary.

minimal_pair.case: A person reveals a secret and then tries to smooth things over afterward.
minimal_pair.why_it_matches: The privacy decision is already over; the real task is repair, so this unit should not be used.

boundary_stress_test: If the audience is polite but not entitled to know, keep the information private.
If the person asks for gossip, curiosity alone does not create permission.
If the detail is flattering rather than harmful, it can still be private.
references.generalization_note: This unit covers disclosure boundaries across friendships, family, work, and online settings; the core judgment is always who may know what, not how to fix the aftermath.

validation_seed.positive_pattern: The scene asks whether a private fact may be told to a specific person or group.
validation_seed.near_miss_pattern: The scene asks how to respond after a secret has already been exposed.
validation_seed.boundary_pattern: The scene asks how to look trustworthy or polished by controlling self-disclosure.

notes: Keep the unit narrow: disclosure boundary only.
If the case turns into apology, reputation repair, or impression management, route out.
core_question: Determine what information may be shared and what should remain private
